questions.question: From the alternatives given below, choose the correct meaning of the idiom 'talk nineteen to the dozen'.

options.text: To speak slowly in a whispering tone
To speak in an angry manner
To speak very rapidly, hurriedly, and/or energetically

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option(4)'** i.e. **'To speak very rapidly, hurriedly, and/or energetically'**.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **'talk nineteen to the dozen'** is used to describe someone who is talking very **quickly** and **continuously**, often without stopping. (बहुत तेज़ी से और लगातार बात करना)
 
 
• **Example: **Ever since she returned from her **overseas trip**, she has been **talking nineteen to the dozen** about her experiences.
 
 
 
• **'To speak very rapidly, hurriedly, and/or energetically'** means to converse at a **fast pace**, possibly due to **excitement**, **nervousness**, or having a lot of information to share at once. (बहुत तेज़, जल्दबाजी में, और उत्साह के साथ बोलना)
 
 
• **Example: **The **commentator** had to **speak very rapidly** to keep up with the **fast-paced action** on the field.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can conclude that the idiom **'talk nineteen to the dozen'** corresponds to the meaning of speaking **energetically** and **hurriedly**.

Therefore, the correct answer is- **To speak very rapidly, hurriedly, and/or energetically**.

**Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To speak slowly in a whispering tone** (फुसफुसाते हुए धीमी आवाज़ में बोलना): This means to talk at a **low volume** and a **measured speed** so as not to be overheard.
 
 
• **Example: **They had to **speak slowly in a whispering tone** while the baby was **napping** in the next room.
 
 
 
• **To whisper in the ear** (कान में फुसफुसाना): The act of speaking **softly** and **directly** into someone’s ear to share a **secret** or private thought.
 
 
• **Example: **She leaned over to **whisper in his ear** so that no one else at the **table** could hear the surprise plan.
 
 
 
• **To speak in an angry manner** (क्रोधित लहजे में बोलना): Communicating with a voice that reflects **displeasure**, **frustration**, or **fury**.
 
 
• **Example: **The **coach** began to **speak in an angry manner** after the team made several **avoidable errors**.

• **Option 2: For** is typically used to indicate **purpose**, **reason**, or **duration** (e.g., 'I bought this for you').

questions.question: Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice? The final report will have been completed by the research team before the board meeting begins.

options.text: The research team will complete the final report before the board meeting begins.
The research team will have completed the final report before the board meeting begins.
The research team completes the final report before the board meeting begins.
The research team has completed the final report before the board meeting begins.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The research team will have completed the final report before the board meeting begins**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **Passive Voice** and follows the **Future Perfect Tense** structure. The passive formula for this tense is: **Subject + will + have + been + past participle (V3) + by + Agent**.
 
• In the given sentence, **the final report** is the subject receiving the action, **will have been completed** is the verb phrase, and **the research team** is the agent (doer of the action).
 
• To convert a **Future Perfect** sentence into the **Active Voice**, the agent of the passive sentence becomes the new subject, and the formula changes to: **Subject + will + have + past participle (V3) + Object**.
 
• Applying the conversion: The agent **the research team** moves to the subject position, the verb phrase changes from **will have been completed** to **will have completed**, and **the final report** becomes the direct object.
 
• The subordinate clause **before the board meeting begins** functions as an adverbial of time and remains unchanged in the transformation from passive to active voice.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Voice and Tense Consistency**:
 
 
• **Future Perfect Tense**: Used to indicate an action that will be completed at some point in the future before another action takes place. It is essential to maintain this tense during voice conversion.
 
• **Active Voice**: It is generally preferred in professional and academic writing because it is more direct, concise, and clearly identifies the **actor** performing the action.
 
• **Incorrect Tense Usage**:
 
 
• Option 1 uses **Simple Future** (will complete), which fails to capture the completed nature of the action relative to the deadline.
 
• Option 3 uses **Simple Present** (completes), which usually denotes facts, habits, or scheduled future events in a different context.
 
• Option 4 uses **Present Perfect** (has completed), which refers to an action finished in the past with current relevance, contradicting the future context of the sentence.
 
 
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice? The lights are to be switched off when you leave.

options.text: You will switch the lights off when you leave.
The lights should be switched off before leaving.
Switch off the lights when you leave.
Switched off the lights when you leave.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Switch off the lights when you leave**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The sentence **'The lights are to be switched off when you leave'** is in the **passive voice**. It uses the **passive infinitive** structure, which consists of **'to be'** followed by the **past participle** (**'switched'**).

• This grammatical structure is commonly employed to state **rules**, **official instructions**, or **formal commands** where the actor is often implied rather than stated.

• To convert an instruction from passive to **active voice**, we generally use the **imperative mood**. In English, imperative sentences are inherently in the **active voice** because the subject **'you'** is understood as the performer of the action.

• An **imperative sentence** begins with the **base form** (infinitive without 'to') of the verb. Thus, **'to be switched off'** becomes **'Switch off'** in the active form.

• The phrase **'when you leave'** is a **subordinate clause** indicating time and remains unchanged in the conversion as it already identifies the actor (**'you'**).

• Therefore, the sentence **'Switch off the lights when you leave'** accurately captures the active voice while maintaining the original **imperative intent** and **temporal context**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Voice and Grammatical Mood**:

• **Active Voice**: The **subject** performs the action denoted by the verb. It is the most **direct** and **efficient** way to communicate instructions in everyday language.

• **Imperative Mood**: A verb mood used to give **orders**, **directions**, or **warnings**. It always utilizes the **present tense** and does not require an explicit subject because it is addressed to a second person.

• **Passive Voice**: Used when the **focus** is on the action or the **object** receiving the action (the **'lights'**) rather than the person performing it.

• **Incorrect Option Analysis**:

• **Option 1**: **'You will switch...'** uses the **future tense** (**'will'**), which changes the tone from a direct instruction to a statement about a future event or a prediction.

• **Option 2**: **'The lights should be switched off...'** incorporates the **modal verb** 'should' but maintains the **passive construction** (**'be switched'**), failing the requirement for active voice.

• **Option 4**: **'Switched off the lights...'** is grammatically flawed as an instruction because it uses the **past participle** or **past tense** form instead of the **base verb** required for an active imperative command.

</ul

questions.question: Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence. Rakesh was very nice _______ Radhika when they last met each other.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**to**'. **__Key Points__** __ 
• The adjective **nice** is followed by the preposition **to** when describing a person's **behavior** or **attitude** toward another person. 
• In the given sentence, the behavior of **Rakesh** is being directed toward **Radhika**, making **to** the grammatically correct choice. 
• Other adjectives that follow this same pattern (**Adjective + to + Someone**) include **kind**, **polite**, **rude**, and **generous**. Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**. **Complete Sentence:** *'Rakesh was very **nice to**__ Radhika when they last met each other.'* **__Additional Information__** 
• **Option 1: 'with'** is typically used to describe how someone handles objects or general situations (e.g., **nice with** his tools), or sometimes to describe general companionship, but **to** is the standard preposition for directed behavior. 
• **Option 2: 'at'** is used to indicate a specific location or proficiency in a skill (e.g., **good at** tennis), which is not applicable here. 
• **Option 4: 'by'** is used to identify the agent of an action or a method, not the recipient of a specific behavior or trait. </ul

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options A, B and C are not found suitable, choose Option D: "No Improvement Required."
The diplomat's speech was intended to pacify tensions, but his ambitious remarks only added fuel in the fire.

options.text: antagonistic remarks only added fuel into the fire
ambiguous remarks only added fuel to the fire
assiduous remarks only added fuel for the fire

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ambiguous remarks only added fuel to the fire**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The sentence requires an idiomatic correction and a contextual vocabulary improvement. The standard English idiom is **add fuel to the fire** (or **flame**), which means to cause a situation to become more **intense**, **excited**, or **uncontrollable**, typically in a negative way. The original phrase **added fuel in the fire** uses the incorrect preposition **in**.

• The word **ambitious** (showing a strong desire for success) does not logically contrast with the intention to **pacify** (to calm or soothe). In a **diplomatic context**, remarks that are **ambiguous** (vague or open to multiple interpretations) are a common cause of escalating **tensions** because they lead to **misunderstanding** and **mistrust**.

• Replacing **ambitious** with **ambiguous** creates a logical transition using the conjunction **but**, indicating that while the **diplomat** intended to resolve the conflict, the **lack of clarity** in his speech achieved the opposite result.

• Option 1 is incorrect because it uses the preposition **into**, which is not the standard form of the idiom, and **antagonistic** implies an intentional **hostility** that contradicts the **intended** goal of the speech.

• Option 3 is incorrect because **assiduous** means showing great care and **perseverance**; such remarks would unlikely result in the worsening of a situation.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Ambiguous**:

• Originates from the Latin **ambiguus**, meaning **doubtful**.

• Key characteristic: It describes a **statement** or **sign** that can be understood in more than one way, often leading to **confusion** in **negotiations** or **legal documents**.

• **Antagonistic**:

• Derived from **antagonismos** (Greek), meaning **struggle**.

• Key characteristic: Shows active **opposition** or **hostility** toward someone or something.

• **Assiduous**:

• Refers to a person or action showing **meticulous** attention and **constant** effort.

• Key characteristic: Highly valued in **academic** and **professional** settings for **thoroughness**.

• **Pacify**:

• To bring **peace** to a state of **turmoil** or **war**.

• Core function: It is a **transitive verb** often used in **international relations** and **conflict resolution**.

</ul

questions.question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.
S1. Babies were frequently exposed to polioviruses. A. Paradoxically, when sanitation improved, infants were no longer exposed at an age when they were protected, so they did not develop antibodies to the viruses. B. The babies then developed their own antibodies to the virus. C. Consequently, when they were exposed to the virus in later childhood and adulthood, they were at risk to contract polio. D. These infants did not contract the disease because their mothers' antibodies were passed on to them through breast-feeding. S2. This understanding about the nature of polio grew through painstaking research over the first half of the twentieth century, much of it funded by the March of Dimes, a grassroot organization founded with the help of President Roosevelt.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph explains the biological and environmental factors that influenced the spread and immunity of **polio** during the 20th century. 
• **Sentence D follows S1** because it provides a reason for the observation in the opening sentence. S1 states that babies were exposed to **polioviruses**, and Sentence D explains why they remained healthy: 
• 'These infants did not contract the disease because their mothers' **antibodies** were passed on to them through **breast-feeding**.' 
• **Sentence B follows next** as it describes the subsequent step in the natural **immunity** process for those infants: 
• 'The babies then developed their own **antibodies** to the virus.' 
• **Sentence A is the third sentence** as it introduces a historical shift. It uses the word 'paradoxically' to show how **improved sanitation** disrupted this natural immunity cycle: 
• 'Paradoxically, when **sanitation** improved, infants were no longer exposed at an age when they were protected, so they did not develop **antibodies** to the viruses.' 
• **Sentence C is the fourth sentence** because it outlines the dangerous consequence of the lack of early exposure mentioned in Sentence A: 
• 'Consequently, when they were exposed to the virus in later childhood and adulthood, they were at risk to contract **polio**.'

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

'**Babies** were frequently exposed to **polioviruses**. These infants did not contract the disease because their mothers' **antibodies** were passed on to them through **breast-feeding**. questions.question: Choose the correct form of the verb to fill in blank (A).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**provides**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ 
• The sentence requires a verb that correctly agrees with the subject '**such content**'. 
• In English grammar, '**content**' is an uncountable noun, which is treated as a **singular subject**. 
• The passage is written in the **simple present tense** to describe general observations and facts. 
• According to the rules of **subject-verb agreement**, a singular subject in the present tense takes a verb ending in '**-s**' or '**-es**'. 
• Therefore, '**provides**' is the grammatically correct form to fill blank (A). Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'. Complete Passage: *Cartoons and fantasy shows have become an inseparable part of childhood. Children today spend hr watching animated characters who fight villains, explore magical lands, or solve mysteries. While such content 1. **provides**__ entertainment and imagination, it also shapes the way children think and behave. Psychologists point out that children often imitate what they see. A child who watches violent cartoons 2. __**may**__ become aggressive, while one who watches educational programs develop problem-solving skills. Thus, the impact is not always negative, but it depends on the type of content consumed. Fantasy worlds encourage creativity, but they can also create unrealistic expectations. If children live too much in imaginary lands, they will struggle to deal 3. __**with**__ real-life challenges. For example, believing that problems disappear magically can prevent them from building resilience. Parents, therefore, play a key role. They should guide children toward shows that are age-appropriate and discuss with them the difference between fiction and reality. A balanced approach is necessary, because neither complete 4. __**prohibition**__ nor unlimited freedom is healthy. As one expert said, 'Cartoons are like fire: they can warm if used wisely or burn if left unchecked.' This metaphor 5. __**shows**__ the double-edged nature of media influence on young minds.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 
• '**Provide**' is the base form used with plural subjects (e.g., 'The programs **provide** information'). 
• '**Will providing**' is a grammatically incorrect construction. The modal '**will**' must be followed by the base verb (e.g., '**will provide**'). 
• '**Provided**' is the past tense or past participle form, which is unsuitable for a passage describing ongoing general truths in the **present tense**. </ul
